mcqs.question: Which criterion is used when all three sides of a triangle are given?
mcqs.correct_answer: C) SSS
mcqs.explanation: SSS stands for Side-Side-Side — the criterion where all three sides of a triangle are known. With all three sides given, a unique triangle can be constructed (if the triangle inequality holds). Draw the base, then use a compass to draw arcs from both endpoints at the other two side lengths — their intersection gives the apex.

mcqs.question: In SAS construction, the given angle must be:
options: A) The largest angle of the triangle
B) The angle between (included by) the two given sides
C) Any angle of the triangle
D) The angle opposite to the longest side
mcqs.correct_answer: B) The angle between (included by) the two given sides
mcqs.explanation: In SAS (Side-Angle-Side), the angle must be the INCLUDED angle — the one between (sandwiched between) the two given sides. It is formed at the vertex common to both given sides. If the angle is not between the two sides, the construction becomes ambiguous (SSA case) and does not uniquely determine the triangle.

mcqs.question: Which criterion applies when two angles and the side between them are known?
mcqs.correct_answer: D) ASA
mcqs.explanation: ASA stands for Angle-Side-Angle. The given side must be the INCLUDED side — the side between (sandwiched between) the two given angles. It connects the vertices where the two given angles are located. In the construction: draw the included side, construct the two angles at each endpoint, extend the rays to meet at the third vertex.

mcqs.question: RHS construction is applicable ONLY to:
mcqs.correct_answer: C) Right-angled triangles
mcqs.explanation: RHS (Right angle-Hypotenuse-Side) is specifically for right-angled triangles. The 'R' stands for the right angle (90°), which must be one of the angles of the triangle. Without the right angle condition, the same information (SSA — side-side-angle) would be ambiguous. The right angle makes the construction uniquely determined through the Pythagorean theorem.

mcqs.question: In a right-angled triangle, the hypotenuse is:
options: B) The side adjacent to the right angle
C) The side opposite the right angle
D) Any one of the three sides
mcqs.correct_answer: C) The side opposite the right angle
mcqs.explanation: The hypotenuse is always the side OPPOSITE the right angle (90°). It is the longest side of a right-angled triangle. In a right-angled triangle ABC with the right angle at B, the hypotenuse is AC (opposite to B). The Pythagorean theorem states: hypotenuse² = sum of squares of the other two sides.

mcqs.question: Which of the following sets of sides CANNOT form a triangle?
mcqs.correct_answer: C) 2 cm, 3 cm, 6 cm
mcqs.explanation: Triangle inequality: sum of any two sides must be > third side. Check 2+3=5, but 5 is NOT greater than 6 (5 < 6). The inequality fails, so no triangle can be formed with sides 2, 3, 6. The other options: 5+6=11>8 ✓; 3+4=7>5 ✓; 7+8=15>9 ✓ — all satisfy the triangle inequality.

mcqs.question: What property is used to construct a line parallel to a given line through an external point?
options: A) Vertically opposite angles are equal
B) Angles in a triangle sum to 180°
C) Alternate interior angles (or corresponding angles) are equal when a transversal cuts parallel lines
D) Exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of remote interior angles
mcqs.correct_answer: C) Alternate interior angles (or corresponding angles) are equal when a transversal cuts parallel lines
mcqs.explanation: The parallel line construction uses the converse of the alternate interior angles theorem: if a transversal makes equal alternate angles with two lines, those lines are parallel. A transversal is drawn from the external point to the given line, the angle is noted, and an equal angle is constructed at the external point to create the parallel line.

mcqs.question: If two angles of a triangle are 60° and 70°, what is the third angle?
mcqs.explanation: Angle sum property: all three angles of a triangle sum to 180°. Third angle = 180° − 60° − 70° = 50°. This is used in ASA construction to verify the third angle after drawing the triangle. Always check that all three angles sum to 180°.

mcqs.question: In triangle ABC, angle B = 90°. Which side is the hypotenuse?
mcqs.correct_answer: C) AC
mcqs.explanation: The hypotenuse is the side OPPOSITE the right angle. Since angle B = 90°, the hypotenuse is the side NOT touching B — which is AC. Sides AB and BC both touch vertex B (they are the legs of the right-angled triangle). AC is opposite to B and is the hypotenuse.

mcqs.question: If three angles of a triangle are given (AAA), how many distinct triangles can be drawn?
mcqs.correct_answer: D) Infinitely many
mcqs.explanation: AAA (three angles given) does NOT uniquely determine a triangle. All triangles with the same three angles are similar — they have the same shape but can have any size. Without at least one side measurement, infinitely many triangles (of different sizes) satisfy AAA. To construct a UNIQUE triangle, at least one side must be known.

mcqs.question: You are given triangle PQR with PQ = 5 cm, QR = 7 cm, and angle Q = 45°. Which criterion applies?
options: A) SSS — all sides are effectively known
B) SAS — two sides and the included angle at Q
C) ASA — two angles and an included side
D) RHS — angle Q is acute, not 90°
mcqs.correct_answer: B) SAS — two sides and the included angle at Q
mcqs.explanation: PQ = 5 cm and QR = 7 cm are two sides. Angle Q = 45° is AT vertex Q — which is the common vertex of sides PQ and QR. Therefore, angle Q is the INCLUDED angle between the two given sides. This is SAS (Side-Angle-Side). RHS requires a 90° angle; SSS requires all three sides; ASA requires two angles and a side.

mcqs.question: To construct triangle ABC where angle A = 55°, AB = 6 cm, angle B = 65°, the construction starts by:
options: B) Drawing AB = 6 cm first, then constructing angles at A and B
D) Finding angle C first, then using SSS
mcqs.correct_answer: B) Drawing AB = 6 cm first, then constructing angles at A and B
mcqs.explanation: This is ASA construction: angle A = 55°, included side AB = 6 cm, angle B = 65°. In ASA, always draw the INCLUDED SIDE first — it is the base of the construction. After drawing AB = 6 cm: construct 55° at A and 65° at B. Extend both rays until they meet at C. Angle C = 180° − 55° − 65° = 60°.

mcqs.question: A right-angled triangle has hypotenuse = 5 cm and one leg = 3 cm. The other leg is:
mcqs.correct_answer: B) 4 cm
mcqs.explanation: Using Pythagoras: leg² + leg² = hypotenuse². 3² + b² = 5². 9 + b² = 25. b² = 16. b = 4 cm. This is the famous 3-4-5 Pythagorean triple. Verify: 3² + 4² = 9 + 16 = 25 = 5² ✓. In RHS construction with hypotenuse = 5 cm and leg = 3 cm, the other leg will measure exactly 4 cm.

mcqs.question: In ASA construction, after drawing the included side and the two angles at each endpoint, what do you do next?
options: A) Measure the third side with a ruler
B) Extend the two angle rays until they intersect — the intersection is the third vertex
C) Draw an arc from each endpoint to find the third vertex
D) Use Pythagoras to calculate the third vertex position
mcqs.correct_answer: B) Extend the two angle rays until they intersect — the intersection is the third vertex
mcqs.explanation: In ASA construction: after drawing the included side and constructing the two given angles at each endpoint, you extend both angle rays (from each endpoint, in the directions given by the angles) until they meet. The point of intersection is the third vertex of the triangle. This is unlike SSS where arcs are used — in ASA, RAYS from the endpoints find the apex.

mcqs.question: Can a triangle be constructed with angles 70°, 60°, and 50°, with NO side given?
options: A) Yes, exactly one triangle is possible
B) No, infinitely many triangles are possible but none is unique
C) No, these angles cannot form a triangle
D) Yes, but only an equilateral triangle
mcqs.correct_answer: B) No, infinitely many triangles are possible but none is unique
mcqs.explanation: Angles 70° + 60° + 50° = 180° ✓ — so triangles with these angles DO exist. However, without any side measurement, infinitely many similar triangles satisfy these angle conditions (with any scale). No UNIQUE triangle can be constructed. This is the AAA case — shape determined but size not fixed.

mcqs.question: While constructing a parallel line using the transversal method, you draw a transversal making an angle of 70° with the given line. What angle must you construct at the external point?
mcqs.explanation: To create a parallel line, you copy the SAME angle at the external point. If the transversal makes 70° with the given line at their intersection, you must construct a 70° angle at the external point on the same side (corresponding angles) OR the alternate angle of 70° on the opposite side (alternate interior angles). Either way, a 70° angle is constructed at the external point.

mcqs.question: Why is SSA (two sides and a NON-included angle) not a reliable construction criterion?
options: A) Because two sides are not enough to determine a triangle
B) Because the construction may yield 0, 1, or 2 valid triangles, making it ambiguous
C) Because SSA always gives the same triangle as SAS
D) Because a non-included angle cannot be measured accurately
mcqs.correct_answer: B) Because the construction may yield 0, 1, or 2 valid triangles, making it ambiguous
mcqs.explanation: SSA (Side-Side-Angle where the angle is NOT between the two sides) is the 'ambiguous case'. When you draw one side, construct the given angle at one endpoint, then swing an arc of the second side length from the other endpoint: the arc may not reach the angle ray (0 triangles), just touch it (1 triangle), or cross it at two points (2 triangles). This ambiguity makes SSA unreliable as a unique construction criterion.

mcqs.question: In triangle XYZ, XY = 8 cm, YZ = 6 cm, and angle X = 40°. Angle X is NOT between XY and YZ (since angle Y is between them). What type of problem is this?
options: A) SAS — angle X is close enough to be considered included
B) ASA — with angle X and side XY given
C) SSA — the ambiguous case, which may not give a unique triangle
D) SSS — all sides can be calculated from this information
mcqs.correct_answer: C) SSA — the ambiguous case, which may not give a unique triangle
mcqs.explanation: Angle X is at vertex X. The two sides are XY = 8 cm (touches X) and YZ = 6 cm (does NOT touch X). So the angle X is NOT between the two given sides (the included angle between XY and YZ is angle Y). This is SSA — a non-included angle — which is the ambiguous case. It may yield 0, 1, or 2 triangles depending on the specific measurements.

mcqs.question: A triangle is to be constructed with sides 6 cm, 6 cm, and angle between them = 80°. After construction, which of the following is true about this triangle?
options: B) It is isosceles with the two equal sides being the given sides
C) It is a right-angled triangle
D) It is a scalene triangle with all different sides
mcqs.correct_answer: B) It is isosceles with the two equal sides being the given sides
mcqs.explanation: This is SAS with two EQUAL sides (6 cm and 6 cm) and an included angle of 80°. A triangle with two equal sides is ISOSCELES. The two given sides (6 cm each) are the equal sides. The base (third side) will be different (calculable by the law of cosines, but not required here). It is NOT equilateral (that would need all three sides equal AND angles 60° each). It is NOT right-angled (80° ≠ 90°).

mcqs.question: You want to construct a triangle with angle A = 40°, angle C = 60°, and the side AC = 7 cm. What criterion applies and what is angle B?
mcqs.correct_answer: B) ASA; angle B = 80°
mcqs.explanation: Angle A = 40° (at vertex A), angle C = 60° (at vertex C), and AC = 7 cm (the side BETWEEN vertices A and C). This is ASA — the side AC is the INCLUDED side between angles A and C. Angle B = 180° − 40° − 60° = 80°. Construction: draw AC = 7 cm, construct 40° at A, construct 60° at C, extend rays to meet at B.
